claims.text: The as-deposited material is a non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloy produced by physical vapor deposition.
The as-deposited alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp, first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited transition produces a large magnetocaloric entropy change and substantial hysteresis.
Annealing at 200–300 °C for 1–2 hours can modify the alloy's defect density.
The low-temperature anneal can modify local short-range chemical order.
Defect density and local chemical order tune magnetostructural coupling.
Magnetostructural coupling governs the magnitude of the magnetocaloric response.
Magnetostructural coupling governs the hysteresis width during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Anti-phase and domain boundaries mediate nucleation and propagation of the magnetostructural transition.
Low-temperature annealing relaxes internal stresses.
Annealing-induced structural relaxation reduces defect-site pinning.
Reduced pinning lowers the energy barrier for the magnetostructural transformation.
A lower transformation barrier enables a smoother and less hysteretic magnetostructural transformation.
Annealing will slightly broaden the magnetostructural transition relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will reduce hysteresis and its associated energy losses relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will preserve a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
The proposed annealing treatment will support faster heat exchange during the cooling cycle.
Annealing at 200–300 °C will avoid unwanted phase changes and excessive grain growth.
The predicted behavior is limited to low applied fields below 1 T and compositions or treatments that do not significantly alter phase constitution.
